questions.q: The area (in square units) of the region enclosed between the parabola $y^2=2 x$ and the line $y=4 x-1$
questions.solution:
Given equation of parabola $y^2=2 x\ldots(\mathrm{i})$ and equation of line $y=4 x-1\ldots(\mathrm{ii})$ Intersecting points of Eqs. (i) and (ii) $\operatorname{are} \left(\frac{1}{8}, \frac{-1}{2}\right)$and $\$left(\frac{1}{2},$1\right)$
Required area $A O B=\int_{-1 / $2}^1 \left(\frac{y+1}{4}-\frac{y^2}{2}\right)$d $y=\frac{1}{4} \int_{-1 / 2}^1($y+1) d $y-\frac{1}{2} \int_{-1 / 2}^1$y^2 d $y=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+$y\right]_{-1 / $2}^1-\frac{1}{2}\$left[\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1 / 22}^1=\frac{1}{4}\left[\$left(\frac{1}{2}+1\right)-\left(\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]-\frac{1}{6}\l$left[1-\left(-\frac{1}{8}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3}{8}\right]-\frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{9}{8}\right)=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{15}{8}-\frac{3}{16}=\frac{15-6}{32}=\frac{9}{32}$sq units$

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $y=9 x^2$ and $y=5 x^2+4$ (in sq units) is
questions.solution:
Intersecting point of $y=9 x^2$ and $y=5 x^2+4$ is given by
$\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow \quad 4 x²=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x²=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x= $\pm$1 \\ & \therefore \quad y=9( $\pm$1)^2=9 \\ & \end{aligned} Hence, intersecting points are $( \pm 1,9)$. $\begin{aligned} \therefore\text { Required area }$& =2 \int_0^1\left[\left($5 x²+4\right)-\left($9 x²\right)\right] d x \\ & =2 \int_0^1\left($4-4 x²\right) d x \\ & =2\left[$4 x-$\frac{4 x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 \\ & =2\left($4-$\frac{4}{3}\right)-($0-0)=2 $\times \frac{8}{3}$\\ & =$\frac{16}{3} \text { sq units } \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The larger of the two areas (in sq. units) into which the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 16a^{2}$ is divided by the parabola $y^{2} = 6ax$, is
questions.solution:
For point of intersection,& $x^{2} + 6ax = 16a^{2}$

$⇒ x = 2a$

$Area = \pi ⋅ {( 4a )}^{2} - 2( {∫}_{0}^{2a}\sqrt{6ax}dx + {∫}_{2a}^{4a}\sqrt{16a^{2} - x^{2}}dx )$

$= 16\pia^{2} - 2{ {( \dfrac{2\sqrt{6a}x ⋅ \dfrac{3}{2}}{3} )}_{0}^{2a} + {( \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16a^{2} - x^{2}} + \dfrac{16a^{2}}{2}\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{4a} )}_{2a}^{4a} }$

$= 16\pia^{2} - 2{ \dfrac{2\sqrt{6a} ⋅ 2\sqrt{2}a\sqrt{a}}{3} + ( 8a^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{π}{2} - ( a ⋅ 2\sqrt{3}a + 8a^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{π}{6} ) ) }$

$= 16\pia^{2} - 2{ \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{3} + \dfrac{8\pia^{2}}{3} - 2\sqrt{3}a^{2} }$

~$= \dfrac{32\pia^{2}}{3} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{3} = \dfrac{4a^{2}}{3}( 8\pi - \sqrt{3} )sq . units$

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $y=8 x-x^2$ and $8 x-4 y+11=0$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of curves are $\begin{aligned}$& y=8 x-x² \\ & 8 x-4 y+11=0 \end{aligned} Eq. (i) can be rewritten as $\begin{aligned}$& y=-\left($x^2-2 $\cdot$4 x+4^2-4^2\right) \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad y=-\left[($x-4)^2-16\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y-16=-(x-4)^2 \\ & \end{aligned} $(x-4)^2=-(y-16)$, which represent a parabola open downward and having vertex at $(4,16)$. Clearly, Eq. (ii) represent a straight line passing through \left(0, \frac{11}{4}\right)$ and \left(-\frac{11}{8}, 0\right)$ Let us find the point of intersection of given curves, for this substitute the value of $y$ from Eq. (i) in Eq. (ii). $\begin{array}{rlrl} \Rightarrow$& 8 x-4\left($8 x-x²\right)+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 8 x-32 x+4 x²+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 4 x²-24 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 4 x²-22 x-2 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 2 x(2 x-11)-1(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } (2 x-1)(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } x =$\frac{1}{2} \text { or } \frac{11}{2} \end{array}$When $x=\frac{1}{2}$, then $y=\frac{15}{4}$ When $x=\frac{11}{2}$, then $y=\frac{55}{4} \quad$ [using Eq. (ii)] Now, required area $=$ Area of shaded region.
=\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}[y($\text { parabola })-$y($\text { straight line })]$d x $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } =\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2} \left[$8 x-x²-\left(\frac{8 x+11}{4}\right)\right]$d x \\ & =$\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left($32 x-4 x²-8 x-11\right) d x \\ & =-$\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left($4 x²-24 x+11\right) d x \\ & =-$\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{4 x^3}{3}-$24 $\frac{x^2}{2}+$11 x\right]_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2} \\ & =-$\frac{1}{4}\left$\{\left[\frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{1331}{8}-$12 $\times \frac{121}{4}+\frac{121}{2}\right]- \left[\frac{1}{6}-3+\frac{11}{2}\right]\right\} \\ \text{ and } =-\frac{1}{4} \left\{\frac{1331}{6}-363+\frac{121}{2}-\frac{1}{6}+3-\frac{11}{2}\right\} \\ \text{ and } =\frac{-1}{4}\left\{\frac{1330}{6}-360+55\right\} \\ \text{ and } =-\frac{1}{4} \left\${\frac{665}{3}-$305\right\} \\ \text{ and } =-\frac{1}{4}\left\${\frac{665-915}{3}\right$\}}=\frac{250}{4 $\$times3}=\frac{125}{6} $\text { sq units } \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area (in square units) of the region enclosed by the two circles $x^2+y^2=1$ and $(x-1)^2+y^2=1$ is
questions.solution:
Intersection point of two circles
$x^2+y^2=1\ldots$ (i) $(x-1)^2+y^2=1\ldots$ (ii) is given by $(x-1)^2+\left(1-x^2\right)=1\Rightarrow \quad x^2+1-2 x-x^2=0\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{1}{2}$ From Eq. (i), $\frac{1}{4}+y^2=1y^2=1-\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow y= \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ Point $A $\$left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) and $C \left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ So, Area of region $O A B C O=2 \times$ Area of region $O A B D O$ Area of $O A B D O=$ Area of $O A D O+$ Area of $A B D A=\int_0^{1 / 2} \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2} d x+\int_{1 / 2}^1 \sqrt{1-x^2} d x=\left[\frac{1}{2} \cdot(x-1) \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x-1}{1}\right)\right]_0^{1 / 2}+\left[\frac{1}{2} x \sqrt{1-x^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\right]_{1 / 2}^1=\left[-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \cdot 0-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(-1)\right]+\left[\frac{1}{2} \cdot 0+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)-\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]=\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\sin ^{-1}(1)-\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}= $\$left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) from Eq. (i), Area of region $O A B C O=2 \times \left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)=\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

questions.q: If the area of the region bounded by $y=\cos x$, $y=\sin x, x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ and $x=\pi$ is bisected by the line $x=a$, then $\sin \left(a+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=$
questions.solution: According to the question, $\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^a(\sin x-\cos x) d x=\int_a^\pi(\sin x-\cos x) d x\begin{aligned} {[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^a } & =[-\cos x-\sin x]_a^\pi \\ -\cos a & -\sin a+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=1+\cos a+\sin a \\ \sqrt{2}-1 & =2(\cos a+\sin a) \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2} & =\sin a+\cos a \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin a+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos a \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\sin a \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{4}+\cos a \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\sin \left(a+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area enclosed (in square units) by the curve $y = x^{4} - x^{2}$, the $x$-axis and the vertical lines passing through the two minimum points of the curve is
questions.solution:
Given that $y = x^{4} - x^{2}$

For minimum points of curve:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{4} - x^{2}\right) = 0$

$4x^{3} - 2x = 0$

$2x\left(2x^{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2x = 0$~or $2x^{2} - 1 = 0$

$x = 0$~or $x = \dfrac{\pm 1}{2}$

So $f$ is minimum at~$\dfrac{\pm 1}{2}$

The area $= \left|{∫}_{- 1\sqrt{2}}^{1\sqrt{2}}\left(x^{4} - x^{2}\right)dx\right|$

$= \left|2{∫}_{0}^{1\sqrt{2}} \left($x^{4} - x^{2}\right)dx\right| \left[∵ f\left(x\right)\text{is even function}\right]$

$= \left|2 \left[\dfrac{x5}{5} - \dfrac{x3}{3}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$0\right|$

$= \left|2 \left( \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)5 \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$3 $\cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|

$= \left|2\left(\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|

$= \left|\dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|

$= \left|\dfrac{3 - 10}{30\sqrt{2}}\right|

$∴$ Area $= $\dfrac{7}{30\sqrt{2}}

Given curves, $\begin{aligned}$x^{2}+y^{2} &=8...(i)\\ and\quad y^{2} &=2 x...(ii) \end{aligned}
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\therefore\begin{aligned}$x^{2}+2 x-8 &=0 \\ x^{2}+4 x-2 x-8 &=0 \\ x(x+4)-2(x+4) &=0 \\ (x-2)(x+4) &=0 \\ x=2 $\text { and }$y &=$\pm$2 \end{aligned} $\therefore$ Required area $\begin{array}{l} =$2[$\text { Area of }$O A P+$\text { Area of }$P A B] \\ =2\left[\int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{2 x}$d x+\int_{2}^{2 $\sqrt{2}} $\sqrt{8-x^{2}}$d x\right] \\ =2\left[\sqrt{2}\left($x^{3 / 2} $\cdot \frac{2}{3}\right)_{0}^{2}+\left(\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{8-x^{2}}\right.\right.$\\ \left. \left.+\frac{8}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{x}{2 \sqrt{2}}\right)_{2}^{2 \sqrt{2}}\right]\\ =2\left[\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{3}\left(2^{3 / 2}\right)+4 \times \frac{\pi}{2}-2-4 \times \frac{\pi}{4}\right] \eend{array}=2\left[\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{3} \cdot2 \sqrt{2}+2 $\p$pi-2-\pi\rright]=2\left[\ffrac{8}{3}-2+\pi\rright]=2\left(\frac{2}{3}+\pi\right)=2 \pi+\frac{4}{3}$

questions.solution:

On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{aligned} x^{2}-8 x &=0 \\ x(x-8) &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=0,8 \end{aligned}$ and $\quad y=0,8\begin{aligned} \therefore \text { Required area, }(O P A) &=\int_{0}^{8}(\sqrt{8 x}-x) d x \\ &=\left[2 \sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \cdot x^{3 / 2}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{8} \end{aligned}=\frac{4 \sqrt{2}}{3} \cdot(8)^{3 / 2}-\frac{(8)^{2}}{2}=\frac{4 \sqrt{2}}{3} \cdot(2)^{3} \cdot 2 \sqrt{2}-\frac{64}{2}=\frac{16}{3} \times 8-\frac{64}{2}=64\left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=64 \times \frac{(4-3)}{6}=64 \times \frac{1}{6}=\frac{32}{3}$

questions.q: What is the area of loop of the curve $r = asin3\theta$?
questions.solution:
If curve $r = asin3\theta$, to trace the curve, we consider the following table:

$3\theta =$ $0$ $\dfrac{π}{2}$ $\pi$ $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ $2\pi$ $\dfrac{5\pi}{2}$ $3\pi$
$\theta =$ $0$ $\dfrac{π}{6}$ $\dfrac{π}{3}$ $\dfrac{π}{2}$ $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ $\pi$
$r =$ $0$ $a$ $0$ $- a$ $0$ $a$ $0$

Thus, there is a loop between $\theta = 0$~to~$\theta = \dfrac{π}{3}$ and~$r$ varies from $r = 0$~to $r = a$.

~

Hence, the area of the loop lying in the positive
quadrant

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}r^{2}d\theta$

$= \dfrac{a2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\sin^{2}3\thetad\theta$

On putting,~$3\theta = ϕ ⇒ d\theta = \dfrac{1}{3}dϕ$, we get

$= \dfrac{a2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{π}\sin^{2}ϕ \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}dϕ$

$= \dfrac{a2}{6}{∫}_{0}^{π}\sin^{2}ϕdϕ$

$= \dfrac{a2}{6} \cdot 2 \cdot {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\sin^{2}ϕdϕ$

$= \dfrac{a2}{6} \cdot 2 \cdot \dfrac{π}{4}$

$= \dfrac{\pi a2}{12}$& sq. units.
